stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: A core prediction of labor economics is that when the cost of workers rises relative to the cost of machines, firms shift toward machines wherever a task allows it. Economist Dana Okafor applied this reasoning to grocery chains in states that raised their minimum wages between 2015 and 2022. ______ she expected stores facing the steepest wage increases to be the first to install self-checkout lanes, and installation records later confirmed that pattern.
explanation: The first sentence states a principle: costlier workers push firms toward machines. The second says Okafor applied it to grocery chains. The blank sentence gives the expectation she arrived at by doing that. If you put 'so' in the blank, it reads naturally: she applied the principle, so she expected the hardest-hit stores to automate first. 'Hence' expresses that cause-and-result link.

A.why: You took the result of applying the principle for an example of it. The sentence doesn't show one more firm switching to machines. It reports the expectation Okafor drew from the principle, and that expectation follows from it.

C.why: You read a contrast that isn't there. Okafor's expectation agrees with the principle she applied, so nothing needs to be conceded or reversed.

D.why: You picked a time word that puts her expectation before the reasoning that produced it. Her expectation came after she applied the principle, not before.

subtype_name: Result of what came before (Thus / Hence / For this reason / As such)

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Training at high altitude, where each breath delivers less oxygen, prompts the kidneys to release more erythropoietin, a hormone that signals bone marrow to produce red blood cells. After several weeks, an athlete's blood can carry measurably more oxygen than it did at sea level. ______ many endurance coaches schedule a block of altitude training about a month before a major race, timing the return to sea level so the extra red blood cells are still circulating on race day.
explanation: The first two sentences explain how altitude training works and what it does: more red blood cells and blood that carries more oxygen. The last sentence describes a coaching strategy built on that benefit. Coaches schedule altitude blocks because of the mechanism, so 'Consequently' is the right transition.

A.why: You treated the coaches' scheduling as an example of the mechanism. The coaches aren't one more case of the body making red blood cells. They're acting on that fact, so their schedule is a result, not an instance.

B.why: 'Admittedly' concedes a point before a reversal. The passage never turns against the benefit of altitude training. The coaches put it to use.

D.why: You may have been pulled in by the mention of sea level. The coaching strategy doesn't oppose the mechanism. It depends on it.

subtype_name: Result of what came before (Thus / Hence / For this reason / As such)

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Under Halvorsen's 1962 zoning code, every new apartment building had to provide two parking spaces per unit, a rule that could consume a third of a small lot. When city planners studied stalled housing proposals, they found that this requirement, not the price of land, was what made small infill buildings unprofitable. ______ the city council eliminated parking minimums near transit stations in 2019, and permits for small apartment buildings in those areas tripled within four years.
explanation: The first two sentences establish a constraint and a finding: parking minimums, not land prices, were blocking small buildings. The last sentence describes the council's response and what happened next. The council acted because of the planners' finding, so 'Accordingly' gives the right cause-and-result link.

B.why: You treated the council's decision as an example of the planners' finding. It isn't another case of parking rules blocking construction. It's the action taken because of that finding.

C.why: You may have reacted to 'not the price of land' and expected a reversal. Repealing the rule doesn't defy the finding. It follows from it.

D.why: 'Likewise' signals a parallel point. The repeal isn't similar to the finding. It's what the city did in response.

subtype_name: Result of what came before (Thus / Hence / For this reason / As such)

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: A radiosonde is a battery-powered instrument package that rises beneath a weather balloon, recording temperature, humidity, and pressure every second from launch until the balloon bursts roughly 30 kilometers up. Unlike a satellite, which infers these values from radiation it detects from orbit, a radiosonde directly measures the air it passes through. ______ it serves as the reference standard against which meteorologists check satellite temperature estimates.
explanation: The first two sentences describe what a radiosonde is: an instrument that measures the air directly instead of inferring values from a distance. The last sentence says what role it plays because of that, as the standard for checking satellite estimates. 'As such' fits because the sentence assigns the radiosonde a role as a direct result of what it was just described as.

A.why: You treated the radiosonde's role as an example of direct measurement. The last sentence doesn't give one more case of the radiosonde measuring air. It states the role that follows from measuring that way.

B.why: You carried over the contrast in 'Unlike a satellite.' The comparison has already been made inside the second sentence. The last sentence builds on it and doesn't reverse it.

C.why: 'Meanwhile' signals something happening at the same time or a separate thread. The reference-standard role isn't a separate event. It follows from how the radiosonde measures.

subtype_name: Result of what came before (Thus / Hence / For this reason / As such)

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In 2023, ecologist Inés Paredes marked 60 frogs in Larch Pond, released them, and a week later captured 100 frogs, 15 of which carried her marks. In this mark-recapture method, the share of marked animals in a second sample reflects what fraction of the whole population the first sample represented. ______ Paredes estimated that the pond held about 400 frogs, since her 60 marked frogs appeared to make up 15 percent of its population.
explanation: The first sentence gives Paredes's data. The second gives the principle for interpreting it. The last sentence gives the estimate she reached by applying that principle to her data: 15 of 100 is 15 percent, and 60 is 15 percent of 400. Her estimate follows from the principle, so 'Thus' is correct.

A.why: You mistook the result of applying the principle for an example of it. Paredes's study was already the case under discussion. The last sentence isn't a new example. It's the conclusion her data and the principle lead to.

C.why: 'Still' signals that something holds despite what came before. Her estimate agrees with the method and her data. Nothing pushes against it.

D.why: 'Likewise' introduces a parallel point. The estimate isn't similar to the principle. It's the result of using it.

subtype_name: Result of what came before (Thus / Hence / For this reason / As such)
